shorts.title: What you will learn: Move semantics
shorts.hook: Move the data. Do not copy it.
shorts.script: Move the data. Do not copy it. Today we learn to move data. A move hands over the data instead of copying it, so big objects stay fast. A copy makes a second set of data. A move hands the data to the new owner, and leaves the old owner empty. Think of handing over the keys of a house. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: What you will learn: Move semantics.

shorts.title: Move semantics in one minute
shorts.hook: A copy makes a second set of data.
shorts.script: A copy makes a second set of data. A move hands the data to the new owner, and leaves the old owner empty. Think of handing over the keys of a house. You do not build a second house. Vector a owns three numbers on the heap. Move does not move anything by itself. It marks a as safe to steal from. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Move semantics in one minute.

shorts.title: Inside the second program
shorts.hook: Two ampersands make an rvalue reference.
shorts.script: Two ampersands make an rvalue reference. This is the move constructor. It copies only the pointer. Then it sets the old pointer to null, so the old object frees nothing. We delete the copy constructor, because a copy would be wrong here. This line calls the move constructor. The output is made, moved, and then one hundred and zero. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Inside the second program.

shorts.title: Bug of the Day: Copying a unique pointer
shorts.hook: Can you spot the bug in move semantics?
shorts.script: Can you spot the bug in move semantics? Bug of the Day. We copy a unique pointer. The compiler says the copy constructor is deleted. One owner only. Use move to hand over the ownership. A unique pointer has one owner only, so it cannot be copied. Move it to give the ownership to another pointer. A copy duplicates the data. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Bug of the Day: Copying a unique pointer.

shorts.title: Pun and challenge
shorts.hook: Can you move a string into a vector in move semantics?
shorts.script: Can you move a string into a vector in move semantics? Why did the string move out? It wanted its own space, with no copies. Make a string, and push it into a vector of strings with move. Print the vector size. Write your answer in the comments. A copy duplicates the data. A move hands over the data. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Pun and challenge.
